text: Remove long instructional/explanatory paragraphs and header description blocks from operational screens.
Move useful explanations into the existing accessible contextual-help “!” control.
Make page/help titles clickable where appropriate and apply the same pattern consistently.
Preserve essential validation messages, warnings, statuses, audit information, and legal/accounting notices. Do not hide information required to complete or approve a transaction.
Fix the sidebar so its final items remain reachable by scrolling on desktop and mobile, including browser zoom and short viewport heights.
Preserve keyboard-first operation, Tab order, Enter actions, focus visibility, RTL, Cairo font, accessibility, permissions, and ar/en/ar-EG.
Remove the marked explanatory blocks from Payment Methods and Taxes pages.
Provide compact, consistent Add/Edit Payment Method modals.
Ensure the product form visibly contains a product-specific tax selector.
Product-specific tax overrides the company default; if none is assigned, use the active company default.
“Prices include tax” must only control inclusive versus exclusive calculation. Preserve historical invoice tax snapshots and accounting behavior.
Keep tax validity dates operational in backend validation but hidden from normal UI.
Keep timezone configuration only in General Settings.
Preserve independent continuous numbering per company, branch, and document type without annual reset.

Generate document references using:
    branch code + document type code + zero-padded sequence
    Example: CAI-PO-000001
Show the friendly branch name beside the generated reference in the UI.
Do not replace stored immutable references or renumber existing documents.
Preserve row-lock and concurrency protection.
Keep one clear sidebar destination for the unified Printers and Print Templates screen; remove duplicate navigation entries that open the same page.
Cover all 15 supported print document types.
Replace the printer/template card layout with a compact accessible table consistent with the purchase-invoice tables.
Show assigned printer names and scope instead of only an unexplained assignment count such as “2 printers”.
Remove duplicated printer-management sections.
Preserve existing printer configurations, template data, scope resolution, permissions, and backend behavior.
Remove distributed PDF/XLSX export actions and the large filter block from the Products screen. Exports must remain available through the centralized Reports and Export Center.
Keep only the relevant Add Product and Excel Import actions on the product screen.
Remove the introductory definition block from the product form and put its useful content in contextual help.
Preserve main/subcategory indication and supplier selection.
Keep number-spinner controls removed from cost and selling-price fields.

Repair recoverable product drafts completely:
    - A product saved with incomplete data must persist as Draft.
    - It must appear in the product list with a clear Draft badge.
    - It must provide a visible Resume/Complete Data action.
    - Existing incomplete products, including records identified as 555 and 666, must be discoverable and resumable if present.
    - Draft products must be searchable by saved name, code, barcode, model number, and supplier identifier where data exists.
    - Draft products must not become sellable, purchasable, posted, or active until required validation passes.
Keep active-product search separate from draft-management search where transaction safety requires it.

Add concise contextual help explaining product cards and branch pricing:
    branch selling prices come from the price list assigned to that branch, with a clearly shown fallback if configured.
Do not alter product codes after creation and do not guess a supplier-based code-generation rule.
Repair all downloadable XLSX templates so they open correctly in current Microsoft Excel and contain valid workbook structure, columns, and sample guidance.
Check the other system XLSX templates for the same corruption mechanism and repair the shared generator rather than patching one file only.

Redesign the opening-inventory workflow as a compact full-page stock-addition document similar to a standard inventory addition voucher:
    document header, branch/store, reference, date, product-entry grid, quantities, costs where applicable, totals, notes, status, save draft, resume, approve/post, and reversal history.
Preserve manual entry, paste code/quantity, and XLSX import.
Make pasted rows validate duplicates, unknown products, invalid quantities, and branch/store access before posting.
Explain ecommerce product assignment and “Start without opening stock” through contextual help.
“Start without opening stock” must safely complete initialization with zero balances and must not create fake stock movements.
Preserve immutable posted documents, audited reversal behavior, numbering, permissions, tenant isolation, and transaction safety.
Ensure Customers is visible in the sidebar for authorized users and has correct active-state behavior.
Remove distributed PDF/XLSX export actions from Customers and Customer Groups; retain exports in the central Reports and Export Center.
Change Customer Group add/edit from inline row editing to the same compact modal/full-form convention used elsewhere.
Ensure every customer has a company-scoped customer code with safe uniqueness. Reuse existing data/model support if already present; do not duplicate columns or create a competing identifier.
Add contextual help explaining loyalty points: earning, redemption, balance, expiry if configured, and audit/history behavior.
Do not change existing loyalty calculations without evidence of a defect.
Standardize Supplier Group create/edit UI with the rest of the system.

Add and display three structured supplier contact sections:
    - Owner: name, phone, email
    - Accountant: name, phone, email
    - Sales representative: name, phone, email
Use the existing Hotfix39 supplier-contact data model where possible. If a schema correction is genuinely required, stop before creating a migration and report the exact minimal schema change.
Hide payment terms from all normal supplier-facing screens only. Preserve existing stored values, backend services, historical documents, and compatibility.
Keep supplier PDF/XLSX exports only in the centralized Reports and Export Center.
Remove camera controls completely from purchase-order product rows and other affected purchase screens.
Preserve hardware barcode scanners, typed barcode input, model number, product code, supplier code, SKU/EAN/UPC/alternate identifier, and dynamic product-name search.

Product lookup must work dynamically after the first useful characters and support Arrow Up/Down, Enter selection, Escape, Tab progression, mouse click, Livewire navigation, morphing, and dynamically added rows.
Selecting a product must populate its identifying data, unit, applicable tax, quantity defaults, and purchase cost.
Recalculate line total and document totals immediately when product, quantity, cost, discount, or tax changes. Never leave a valid line total at zero.
Display the purchase-order reference generated by the branch/document numbering service.

Keep Branch and Receiving Warehouse as separate fields:
    - Branch identifies the branch creating the order.
    - Receiving Warehouse identifies the primary receiving location.
    - Later distribution to other branches/stores must occur through controlled inventory transfer/distribution documents.
Reports must allow counting/filtering purchase orders by creating branch.

Preserve the lifecycle:
    Draft → Submitted for Review → Procurement Manager Approved → Ready to Convert.
Clearly show the current status, allowed next action, responsible permission/role, approval history, and rejection/return reason.
Add clear actions to resume a draft, submit, review, approve, view receiving history, and convert eligible remaining quantities to purchase invoice.
Preserve partial receiving and multiple purchase invoices against one purchase order, with remaining-quantity enforcement and idempotent row-locked processing.
On purchase-order save, create or refresh the private versioned PDF snapshot as appropriate and provide explicit View and Download actions. Do not force an automatic download.
Preserve Arabic, English, and Egyptian Arabic PDF output, Cairo font, RTL, authorization, private storage, immutable snapshots, audit logs, and accounting/inventory integrity.
Keep payment terms hidden from the purchase-order UI while preserving backend values and historical data.
Keep purchase-order create/edit as a full page, not an oversized modal.

Ensure products/barcodes, customers/groups, suppliers/groups, purchase orders by branch, purchase invoices/receiving, opening inventory, and inventory movements are available in the centralized Reports and Export Center.
Remove remaining duplicate/distributed export buttons from those operational screens.
Preserve company/branch scope, permissions, filter snapshots, formula-injection protection, job deduplication, export history, and CSV/XLSX/PDF support.
Confirm /reports works in ar, en, and ar-EG without Stringable translation errors.
